description.short_caption: Blood smear showing intracellular ring forms in red blood cells.
description.detailed_description: This image is a stained peripheral blood smear showing multiple red blood cells. One cell contains intracellular ring forms with a central vacuole and chromatin dots, suggestive of a parasitic infection such as Plasmodium species. The smear is stained, likely with Giemsa or Wright stain, to highlight the morphology of the red blood cells and the intracellular parasites.
visible_findings: red blood cells with normal morphology
intracellular ring forms in one red blood cell
stain highlights chromatin dots and vacuoles
reveal_triggers: ring forms in red blood cells

description.short_caption: Peripheral blood smear showing intraerythrocytic ring forms.
description.detailed_description: This is a high-power microscopic image of a peripheral blood smear stained with Giemsa or a similar stain. Numerous red blood cells are visible, with one cell prominently containing intraerythrocytic ring forms, consistent with Plasmodium species. The smear also shows normal red blood cell morphology without significant anisocytosis or poikilocytosis. No visible leukocytes are present in this field.
visible_findings: red blood cells with normal morphology
absence of leukocytes in this field
